summary: edge header attrition evicts version pin causing silent fallback to degraded variant during canary burst
description:
Issue summary: During a staged canary rollout for redwood-open-7b-v2 in us-west (customer AcmeHealth) a subset of tenant traffic silently switched to a degraded fallback variant. Impact: ~2-5% of requests from the tenant were routed to the cheaper/degraded variant for several minutes, causing altered completions and a spike in cost for the tenant due to duplicate retries. Environment: prod-us-west, dedicated tenant on enterprise plan. Observed window: 2026-03-10 18:20 - 18:35 UTC.

Observed behavior: Requests that previously held a model version pin were routed to a degraded secondary variant without explicit pin removal in the control plane. Control-plane logs show pin eviction events with reason=header_mismatch and orchestrator marked cohort as unhealthy, triggering fallback policy. Expected behavior: Pins should survive transient edge header mutations (or be reconstructed via session cookie) and not trigger fallback except for true health failures.

Steps to reproduce (internal repro):
1) Use customer tenant token + pre-existing session cookie for pinned version.
2) Send burst of parallel streaming requests (approx 300 RPS for 30s) from a client that simulates an upstream proxy that truncates the X-Tenant-Session header to 64 chars.
3) Observe in routing logs that requests where X-Tenant-Session was truncated show pin-lookup failures and are routed to fallback variant.

Immediate customer impact: Silent degraded outputs observed by AcmeHealth product team; ticket opened after they saw inconsistent model outputs affecting an automated triage flow.

Initial hypothesis: A recent edge proxy configuration change on the customer's side (header size enforcement) started truncating the header used by our pinning algorithm. The pinning logic treats a header mismatch as a lease/affinity violation and triggers cohort eviction during canary weight surge. The canary window's health smoothing then marked the cohort degraded and applied fallback routing.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 18:30 UTC - Triage: Support verified customer timeline and captured request ids from customer logs.
2026-03-10 19:05 UTC - Correlated client-side header truncation events seen in edge logs with pin_eviction events in routing logs.

2026-03-10 19:20 UTC - Reproduced locally by running a synthetic proxy that truncates X-Tenant-Session to 64 bytes. Confirmed that truncated requests hit fallback path immediately after orchestrator's pin check fails.
2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - Engineering review: pin check currently requires exact header match; there is no length-normalization or signed-cookie fallback for this header in the orchestration handoff.
2026-03-11 13:40 UTC - Found recent customer-side change: AcmeHealth rolled out a new gateway filter at 2026-03-10T18:00 which enforces header size limits. Customer confirmed the change during call.
2026-03-11 15:20 UTC - Canary health smoothing logic amplified the effect during a weight increase at ~18:22 UTC, turning transient pin misses into cohort degradation and fallback.
2026-03-12 10:10 UTC - Patch proposal accepted: add header-canonicalization + graceful pin ttl extension, and fall back to signed session cookie when header length mismatch occurs.
comments: Support (Aisha): Thanks for reporting, AcmeHealth team. We're seeing matching pin_eviction events on our side and are investigating. Could you confirm whether you changed any gateway filters around 18:00 UTC?

AcmeHealth (product-ops): Confirmed — we deployed a gateway config that enforces maximum header lengths at 18:00 UTC. We did not expect it to affect your session header. We can roll back but would prefer a platform fix if possible.

SRE (Diego): I've reproduced with a truncated header locally and can see immediate eviction. Short-term workaround: we can enable an explicit tenant-level routing_override to pin the tenant to the promoted variant while engineering implements a fix. Would you like us to enable?
AcmeHealth: Yes please enable the routing_override for the tenant for the next 48h while we test a gateway hotfix. We'll coordinate rollback after you confirm the platform patch.

Eng (Lina Chen): Investigating patch. Two options: 1) accept header canonicalization (normalize/truncate to canonical form) before pin check, 2) change pin-check to tolerate header-length mismatch when a signed session cookie is present. We'll implement 2) to be conservative. PR drafted: routing/pull/4543.
Support (Aisha): Applied customer-requested routing_override at 2026-03-11T17:05 UTC. Observing metrics: pin_eviction events dropped to zero for that tenant and outputs stabilized.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied: tenant-level routing_override pinned AcmeHealth to the primary variant (manual override) at 2026-03-11T17:05 UTC — mitigated customer impact.
Permanent fix: engineering to deploy change to pin-check logic to accept signed-session cookie fallback and relax strict header-length equality. Patch PR #4543 created; target staging rollout 2026-03-15, prod rollout 2026-03-17 pending canary verification.
Follow-ups: update docs to recommend header canonicalization guidance for self-hosted gateways; add automated alert when header-length-truncation spikes for pinned-tenants.
